name: Cows
label: AmRep
lede: Cows came out of Minneapolis in 1986 with a front man who played bugle and dressed in shaving cream, mousetraps and stuffed animals. They made nine albums, eight of them on [[Amphetamine Reptile Records]], and ended with one produced by the Melvins' Buzz Osborne.

eras.title: A rehearsal-room racket finds its front man
eras.text: Cows start in Minneapolis in the mid-1980s and lose their first vocalist within months. In February 1987 Shannon Selberg takes the mic and turns the racket into a stage act.

years.h: The Rutmanis brothers start a band in Minneapolis
years.p: [[Kevin Rutmanis|140e4f42-ff95-470b-af7b-bd4be6e96db7]] and his brother Sandris form Cows with guitarist [[Thor Eisentrager|470a21c4-785a-473a-8b0c-01a0d33156aa]] and [[Norm Rogers|49f6514a-d4e8-4383-8099-56062daf16c4]], whom Wikipedia lists as the first vocalist. Wikipedia dates the start to 1986; Encyclopedia.com says 1985.
years.xp: That first lineup lasts months. Rogers leaves in January 1987 to play drums for the Jayhawks, and the band goes looking for a singer.

years.h: Rogers leaves for the Jayhawks, Selberg picks up the mic
years.p: [[Norm Rogers|49f6514a-d4e8-4383-8099-56062daf16c4]] goes in January 1987 to drum for the Jayhawks. [[Shannon Selberg|f032b603-a6dd-4349-ab47-53ebefc04667]] joins in February as front man, on vocals and bugle.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cows (band) · Trouser Press: Cows · Encyclopedia.com: The Cows
years.h: Taint Pluribus Taint Unum comes out on a Minneapolis label called Treehouse
years.p: Trouser Press hears "a noisy storm of electrified steel wool" on the first album.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists a fifth member in these years, David van der Steen, billed as a 'fifth udder' from 1987 to 1992. Encyclopedia.com says critics at the time dismissed the band as talentless, and prints Eisentrager's answer: "We wanted to do something pretty unconventional."

years.h: Tony Oliveri takes the drum stool and Chow follows
years.p: [[Tony Oliveri|851fd100-d707-4064-b056-f72b124c3b7e]] replaces Sandris Rutmanis, and the Chow 7-inch comes out on Treehouse the same year.

eras.title: Tom Hazelmyer's reptiles take them in
eras.text: Tom Hazelmyer's Amphetamine Reptile Records signs the band, and three albums follow in three years, each a little clearer than the last.

years.h: Daddy Has a Tail! is the first record on Hazelmyer's label
years.p: Trouser Press says the covers are crude and the production "couldn't be worse if the studio had been underwater."
years.xp: Eisentrager's overdriven guitar is the murk everything sits in. The album is the second Cows record, and the first of eight on [[Tom Hazelmyer|d6569a63-5da9-41fa-a5c9-b6b11b496218]]'s AmRep.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cows (band) · Trouser Press: Cows · Encyclopedia.com: The Cows
years.h: Effete and Impudent Snobs climbs out of the murk
years.p: Trouser Press hears far more clarity and focus than on the last one, with "trebly shards of layered guitar and thrusting fuzz bass" and Selberg's distorted vocals up front.
years.xp:
The Slap Back 7-inch also appears on AmRep this year, alongside Minneapolis-area label-mates such as [[Hammerhead|ea15533d-5ea7-4605-85d5-7634c38a6258]] and Hazelmyer's own [[Halo of Flies|3a26de45-4f41-4e28-bdc8-fda60ef0c8d0]].

Encyclopedia.com quotes a critic who heard the Cows' guitars as "a feral racket that sounded as if the guitars were being played with metal files."

years.h: Rogers comes back and Oliveri goes
years.p: [[Norm Rogers|49f6514a-d4e8-4383-8099-56062daf16c4]] returns to the drums, replacing Oliveri, and stays until 1995.

years.h: Peacetika goes chunky and stop-start
years.p: Trouser Press says the band trades some of its twisted humor for more screaming and instrumental noise, in a style "that makes most hardcore punk easy listening."

eras.title: The bugle goes up front
eras.text: The records get better recorded and stranger. Selberg's bugle moves forward in the mix, and his costumes become the thing people write about.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cunning Stunts · Trouser Press: Cows
years.h: Cunning Stunts sounds better than anything before it
years.p: Iain Burgess produces at Mirror Image in Minneapolis, with Rogers on drums and the bugle in the mix. The title is a spoonerism.
years.xp:
The cover alludes to Reid Miles's 1964 design for Eric Dolphy's Out to Lunch!. The album runs 12 tracks and 38:56 and includes a cover of John Barry's Midnight Cowboy.

The Lancaster New Era ranked it among 1992's best, calling it "truly, truly demented and truly, truly beautiful." City Pages later put it among AmRep's greatest releases. MVD Audio reissued it in 2016 on CD and limited blue vinyl.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cows (band) · Wikipedia: Shannon Selberg · Trouser Press: Cows · Encyclopedia.com: The Cows
years.h: The New York Times sees defiance, pain and dark comedy in a mousetrap costume
years.p: Reviewing the band in May 1992, the Times describes Selberg's costumes as merging "defiance, pain and dark comedy." He performs nearly naked in shaving cream, with mousetraps on his ears, and in suits made of stuffed animals and love dolls.
years.xp:
Trouser Press adds fake-fur football uniforms and business suits with stuffed animals, faces drawn on in marker. The Detroit Metro Times called Selberg a "demented roadside attraction."

Wikipedia describes the shows as raucous: front-row kicks, spitting, thrown mic stands, thrown food. On his own skin Selberg carries a game of Hangman spelling out an obscenity, and an anchor with DAD above it. His line on all of it, as Encyclopedia.com prints it, ends: "The desire to put on a good show."

years.cap: Flyer for Cows and Janitor Joe, all ages, 412 1/2 Soundstage, Minneapolis, June 5, 1993
years.h: Sexy Pee Story turns on betrayal
years.p: Trouser Press says the album widens its subject matter to betrayal in several parts of life, without letting the music ease off.

years.cap: Selberg on bugle, Lee's Palace, Toronto, April 18, 1995
yt: Pickled Garbage Soup, live on local TV show "what.", 1995
years.h: Cow Island 7-inch arrives next to Orphan's Tragedy
years.p: The single lands on AmRep alongside the album. Wikipedia dates Orphan's Tragedy to 1994 and Trouser Press to 1995.
years.xp: Trouser Press is mixed on both Orphan's Tragedy and the album after it, Whorn.

eras.title: A new drummer and a last record
eras.text: Norm Rogers leaves, Freddy Votel steps in, Selberg lives in New York, and the band signs off with an album produced by the Melvins' front man.

yt: Cows live at Lee's Palace, Toronto, April 18, 1995
years.h: Freddy Votel becomes the fourth drummer
years.p: [[Freddy Votel|6340eac7-8561-4e1d-abee-6b3798cfbe55]] replaces Rogers. Encyclopedia.com says the band stays together even with Selberg living in New York.

years.h: Old Gold 1989-1991 collects the first AmRep years
years.p: The compilation gathers the first stretch on the label. Wikipedia dates it 1995, Trouser Press 1996.

years.cap: Cows on the insert for a tape of their CBGB show, New York, June 8, 1996
years.h: Whorn hands the melody to the bugle
years.p: Trouser Press says the bugle sometimes replaces guitar as the main melodic voice.
years.xp: Trouser Press is mixed on it, as on Orphan's Tragedy.

years.src: Wikipedia: Sorry in Pig Minor · Trouser Press: Cows · Encyclopedia.com: The Cows
years.h: King Buzzo produces the last Cows record, Sorry in Pig Minor
years.p: Buzz Osborne of the [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]] produces the ninth album at AmRep Recording Division in Minneapolis (AMREP 066). It runs 47 minutes.
years.xp:
The closing track Say Uncle runs 13:17. It ends at 5:44, followed by about five minutes of silence, then a rough dub remix and an improvised country song with studio banter.

Encyclopedia.com hears Latin and jazz colors in the punk. Trouser Press calls the album "a prolonged symphony in adrenalized guitar wang."

years.h: Eisentrager is worn out from touring, and the band ends
years.p: According to Wikipedia, [[Thor Eisentrager|470a21c4-785a-473a-8b0c-01a0d33156aa]] leaves after the ninth album, citing exhaustion from the road, and the rest disband soon after. Kevin Rutmanis moves on to the [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]].

eras.title: Afterlives
eras.text: Members scatter into other bands, the label keeps the records in print, the band gets a star on the wall of First Avenue, and Rogers dies in 2018.

years.h: Selberg moves to New York and joins The Heroine Sheiks
years.p: [[Shannon Selberg|f032b603-a6dd-4349-ab47-53ebefc04667]] joins the New York noise-rock group on keyboards. Pitchfork called him "the Crispin Glover of the noise rock community."

years.h: Kevin Rutmanis plays bass for the Melvins until 2005
years.p: Wikipedia lists [[Kevin Rutmanis|140e4f42-ff95-470b-af7b-bd4be6e96db7]] in the [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]] from 1998 until June 2005, and on the first two Tomahawk albums, the self-titled debut and Mit Gas.

years.cap: Selberg in a solo set, AmRep 25th Anniversary, Grumpy's, Minneapolis, August 28, 2010
years.h: Cows and the Melvins split Volume 2 of the Sugar Daddy Live series
years.p: AmRep pairs the band with the [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]] on the second volume of its Sugar Daddy Live Split Series.

years.h: The Cunning Stunts demos come out as Stunning Cunts
years.p: Two volumes appear on AmRep, in 2014 and 2015, the first made of demos from the Cunning Stunts sessions.

years.h: Norm Rogers dies of cancer
years.p: The Current reported that the Cows and Jayhawks drummer died in February 2018 after a terminal diagnosis. He had been a manager at Brit's Pub in Minneapolis.
years.xp:
Rogers drummed on the Jayhawks' 1986 self-titled debut and on Cows' Cunning Stunts. At a farewell gathering at Brit's, he posted on his GoFundMe page: "My heart is full and I thank so many people for that!"

He added that he'd had "a helluva life for a lad from small-town Western Minnesota."
